name: The Stones of the Morning Shadow
region_detail: A low ridge among dry hills beyond the northern desert margin.
site_type: stone circle | Ancient sites; supernatural sites | Ancient stone circle and possible instrument for locating water.
history: A circle of pale stones was erected upon the ridge by unknown builders. Old Qasari route maps identify the monument and warn against disturbing its arrangement. Accounts suggest that the stones were once employed to locate an underground source of water, although the method has not survived in common knowledge.
current_state: All of the principal stones remain standing. During particular weeks of the year, their shadows extend eastward regardless of the sun’s position. Outside these periods, the monument behaves ordinarily. No recent excavation has established the location or condition of the purported water source.
inhabitants: Desert wildlife and occasional travelers. No permanent or supernatural inhabitants are established.
danger_level: Low ordinarily; uncertain if the stones are disturbed or the indicated underground location is explored.
points_of_interest:
Circle of pale stones; shallow directional carvings; central patch of exposed bedrock; views of surrounding dry hills; anomalous eastward shadows during certain weeks.

Unresolved elements: The builders and original function of the stone circle; The weeks during which its shadows become anomalous; How the arrangement indicates the location of water; Whether the water source is independent of the disputed ancient watercourse.
discovery: A low ridge among dry hills beyond the northern desert margin. An old Qasari route map depicts the circle and its warning. Desert guides may recognize the ridge, but interpreting the shadow phenomenon requires observation or further study.
related_records:
Rumor: R-RV-019 — The Place Where Shadows Point East — Direct. The monument is the circle described by Qasari travelers.

Notable individuals and factions: Qasari routekeepers and travelers familiar with older maps; Ilyen Seret (N-053) — may recognize aspects of the carvings without necessarily knowing the site’s location.
